Scene headings start with INT., EXT., or a period. The Italian EST. prefix is also supported. Written out in full, they are read as Action.
Forse serve una nuova scena: You may need a new scene
» indicates a change of time or location. In a screenplay, each change starts a new scene with its own heading (e.g. INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT).

Transizione letta come personaggio: Transition read as a character cue
Inquadratura letta come personaggio: Shot read as a character cue
Una riga tutta in maiuscolo seguita subi: An uppercase line immediately followed by other text is read as a character cue. A shot is Action: put “!” in front (hidden on the page), or leave a blank line after it.
La parentetica va sotto il nome: The parenthetical goes below the name
Accanto al nome vanno solo le estensioni: Only technical extensions such as (V.O.) or (O.S.) go beside the name. Delivery directions, such as (
), vanno su una riga a sé, sotto il nome: ), go on their own line, below the name and above the dialogue.
Parentetica in fondo alla battuta: Parenthetical at the end of a speech
Una parentetica non chiude mai una battu: A parenthetical never ends a speech: it describes how the next line is delivered. If it is an action that happens afterward, write it as Action below the dialogue.
L’estensione va accanto al nome: The extension goes beside the name
(V.O.) e (O.S.) non sono parentetiche: s: (V.O.) and (O.S.) are not parentheticals. Write them on the same line as the name, e.g. “MARCO (V.O.)”.
Quando una battuta prosegue alla pagina: When dialogue continues onto the next page, ScripToti adds (MORE) and (CONT’D) automatically. Remove the manually typed marker.
Il simbolo ^ dopo il nome affianca la ba: The ^ symbol after a name places its dialogue beside the preceding speech. There is no preceding speech here. Remove ^ or write the other speech first.
Nessuna voce trovata. Prova con altre pa: No topics found. Try different words, or use “Ask ScripToti” below.
Riga che inizia con INT. / EST. / EXT. /: A line starting with INT. / EXT. / I/E or MONTAGE, or with a leading “.”. The Italian forms EST. and MONTAGGIO are also recognized.
